name: mergeKSortedLists
description: Use a min-heap of size K — one entry per list. Repeatedly extract the smallest element, add it to the result, and insert the next element from that list into the heap.
aim: Merge K sorted linked lists into one sorted linked list in O(N log K) time, where N is the total number of elements and K is the number of lists.
howItWorks: Initialize min-heap with the first element of each of the K lists
Extract minimum from heap → add to result list
Insert the next element from the same list into the heap
Result is a single sorted list with all N elements

time.averageCase: Each element enters/leaves K-size heap once

complexity.spaceDescription: Min-heap stores at most K elements

realWorld: Database merge joins: merging sorted runs in external sort
Log aggregation: merging K time-sorted log files
Search engines: merging sorted posting lists from multiple shards
whenToUse: External sorting when data doesn't fit in RAM
alternatives: Divide and conquer merge: O(N log K) same complexity, recursive
Naive merge all then sort: O(N log N) — worse when K is small

inputHint: One list per row, rows separated by "/". Each row is sorted first.
